The [link functions](#def-link-function) listed in the structure of a [GLM](#def-glm) are not all on the same footing.
For each outcome distribution, the form of its density singles out one link.
To say which, we need the density's *natural parameter*.

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#def-exponential-dispersion-family}
#### Exponential dispersion family

A distribution belongs to the **exponential dispersion family**
if its [density](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pdf) (or [probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf)) can be written as

$$
f(y; \theta, \phi)
= \expf{\frac{y\,\theta - b(\theta)}{\phi} + c(y, \phi)}
$$

for some functions $b(\cdot)$ and $c(\cdot, \cdot)$
[@dobson4e, Chapter 3;
@dunn2018generalized, Chapter 5].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#def-natural-parameter}
#### Natural parameter

In an exponential dispersion family (@def-exponential-dispersion-family),
the parameter $\theta$ is the **natural parameter**
[@dobson4e, Chapter 3;
@dunn2018generalized, Chapter 5].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#def-dispersion-parameter}
#### Dispersion parameter

In an exponential dispersion family (@def-exponential-dispersion-family),
the parameter $\phi > 0$ is the **dispersion parameter**
[@dobson4e, Chapter 3;
@dunn2018generalized, Chapter 5].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-variance-function}
#### Variance function

In an exponential dispersion family (@def-exponential-dispersion-family), $V(\mu) \eqdef b''(\theta)$,
written as a function of $\mu \eqdef b'(\theta)$,
is the **variance function**.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

{{< include _subfiles/Intro-to-GLMs/_exm-variance-function.qmd >}}

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-variance-function-variance}
#### The variance function and the variance

By @thm-edf-mean-variance and @def-variance-function,
$\Varf{Y} = \phi\, V(\mu)$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-canonical-link}
#### Canonical link

In an exponential dispersion family (@def-exponential-dispersion-family),
the **canonical link** is the link function $g(\cdot)$ (@def-link-function)
that sets the [linear predictor](#def-linear-predictor) equal to the natural parameter:
$g(\mu) \eqdef \theta$
[@dobson4e, Chapter 3;
@dunn2018generalized, Chapter 5].
:::
